## Purpose and Entry Points
`discord.py` is an async Python 3.8+ client library for Discord’s HTTP, Gateway, interaction, webhook, and voice APIs. Consumers primarily import `discord`, subclass/use `discord.Client`, or use the commands extension. Package and CLI entry points are `discord/__init__.py` and `discord/__main__.py`; distribution metadata is in `pyproject.toml` and `setup.py`.

## Client Lifecycle and Gateway
`discord/client.py` owns application-facing client lifecycle: token startup, event dispatch, connection state, and shutdown. `discord/gateway.py` implements Discord Gateway WebSocket protocol handling; `discord/shard.py` adds sharded gateway coordination. The control path is client startup → HTTP authentication/session setup → gateway connect/identify/resume → inbound dispatch into client handlers and state.

## HTTP Transport and Rate-Limit Boundary
`discord/http.py` is the REST transport boundary to Discord APIs, including request construction, authentication, response handling, and rate-limit behavior. `discord/webhook/async_.py` and `discord/webhook/sync.py` provide webhook-specific async and synchronous transport surfaces. This layer isolates external Discord REST calls from higher-level domain objects.

## State and Domain Model Hydration
`discord/state.py` maintains cached client state and translates incoming Gateway/HTTP payloads into public Python objects. Core resource models—including guilds, channels, messages, users, members, roles, and permissions—live in `discord/guild.py`, `discord/channel.py`, `discord/message.py`, `discord/user.py`, `discord/member.py`, and `discord/role.py`. Raw protocol shapes are explicitly separated in `discord/types/`, preserving a boundary between Discord JSON payloads and rich API models.

## Commands and Application Commands
`discord/ext/commands/bot.py` layers a bot runtime over `Client`: prefix-command registration, invocation, cogs, checks, converters, and contexts. `discord/ext/commands/core.py` supplies command abstractions and dispatch behavior. Native Discord application-command support is parallel but distinct in `discord/app_commands/tree.py`, `discord/app_commands/commands.py`, and `discord/app_commands/transformers.py`: commands are declared, synchronized with Discord, then interactions are resolved and invoked.

## Interactions and UI Components
`discord/interactions.py` represents incoming interaction workflows; `discord/components.py` models Discord component payloads. `discord/ui/view.py` manages stateful component views and dispatch; concrete controls such as `discord/ui/button.py`, `discord/ui/select.py`, and `discord/ui/modal.py` map user actions to callbacks. This is the boundary for Discord-driven UI state and interaction responses.

## Voice and Media
Voice support is optional and depends on PyNaCl plus system build libraries. `discord/voice_client.py` coordinates voice connections, `discord/player.py` handles audio playback sources/players, and `discord/opus.py` interfaces with Opus encoding. Gateway and voice protocols are separate from standard REST message operations.

## Runtime, Documentation, and Delivery
The library runs on Python `async`/`await` and communicates with Discord’s REST, Gateway/WebSocket, interaction, webhook, and optional voice services. API documentation is built from `docs/`, with public API structure in `docs/api.rst` and extension docs in `docs/ext/commands/`. CI workflows under `.github/workflows/` build, lint, test, and manage Crowdin translations.
